newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude up in line, eyes on Wilmington.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude up in line, eyes on Wilmington.

text.p: - Crude prices on the West Coast rose in line with futures prices in New York, with regional benchmark Alaska North Slope for December delivery notionally up about 50 cents a barrel at $22.10/$22.30 a barrel by midday PST.

Crude dealers on the West Coast said there was little in the way of cash trading in the early session and they said the market tone depended on what happens with Texaco's Wilmington plant, which had a fire early last week.
"We don't know yet what is happening at Wilmington, how hard they are working on it. But there haven't yet been any signs of them backing crude out," said one trader.

The Wilmington refinery, which had a fire on Monday, November 11, has brought all units back to full operation except a damaged hydrotreater, which has a 33,000 bpd capacity. Traders said it is still unclear what the downed unit has done to Texaco's throughput.
"They may have done some time swaps with other refineries but if they have to back some (crude) out it will show soon enough," said a trader at a West Coast refiner.

Other relatively liquid grades were quoted at steady prices with no new deals reported. Kern River was at flat to 10 cents above posted prices, or around $16.70/90, while Line 63 was seen at 95 cents to $1.00 above posted or $21.20/$21.50.
